description: Iranian nationality law is principally patrilineal: a child of an Iranian father is Iranian regardless of birthplace.
notes: Well established in outline; cite the Civil Code article directly before relying on it.

description: A son born abroad to an Iranian father is, in Iranian law, an Iranian male - and therefore in principle liable for military service if he ever enters Iran on an Iranian passport.
energy_note: Passing on a liability you fled, to a child who has never been there.
notes: Enforcement against the never-resident is unclear and varies. Layer-5 target: consular practice for foreign-born sons.

aspect: The asymmetry runs the other way for mothers
description: Until a 2019 reform, Iranian women could not pass nationality to children of foreign fathers. Recording this because the dataset should be accurate about gender rather than one-directional: some Iranian gender burdens fall on women, and this one did.
notes: Included deliberately for balance and credibility.

aspect: SCENARIO - the son born in Toronto
description: Omid's son is born in Toronto in 2028. Under Iranian law he is an Iranian male through his father. If he ever enters Iran on an Iranian passport he is, in principle, a conscript. Omid registers the birth at the consulate anyway, because not doing so means the boy could never inherit the Tehran apartment.
energy_note: Passing on the trap, because refusing to costs him something else.
